Weekly non-parametric temporal base value

Source: R/temporal_base.R
temporal_base_weekly.Rd

Estimates a periodic (7-day) background multiplier from event days-of-week, following the weekly block of the original Zhuang & Mateu (2019) style script: bin events by day-of-week with hist.weighted(), smooth with ker.smooth.fft(), and normalize to a mean of 1. Generalizes both the Loop-0 initial guess (resp_weight = NULL) and the Loop-k E-step re-estimation (resp_weight = the EM responsibility weight for the weekly component at each event, e.g. weekly.fun(days) * mub.events / lambda.at.events in the original script) into one function.

Usage

temporal_base_weekly(
  events,
  resp_weight = NULL,
  breaks = seq(0, 7, 0.05),
  bandwidth = 1
)

Arguments

events

A "semihawkes_events" object from prepare_events().

resp_weight

Optional numeric vector, one entry per event in events$events, e.g. an EM E-step responsibility weight. If NULL (default), only the day-count correction weight is used (the Loop-0 initial-guess behaviour).

breaks

Numeric grid of day-of-week bin edges; default seq(0, 7, 0.05) (0 = Sunday), matching the original script.

bandwidth

Gaussian smoothing bandwidth passed to ker.smooth.fft(); default 1.

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_temporal_base" with elements breaks, basevalue (normalized to mean 1), period (7), and fun (a vectorized function of days returning the periodic multiplier).

References

Zhuang & Mateu (2019); see spHawkes-package.

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date")
weekly <- temporal_base_weekly(ev)
weekly
#> <semihawkes_temporal_base>
#>   Grid points : 141 (range 0 to 7)
#>   Period      : 7
#>   Base value  : mean 1, range [0.839, 1.2]
# Multiplier for each day of the week (0 = Sunday)
round(weekly$fun(0:6), 2)
#> [1] 1.19 1.04 0.88 0.85 0.91 0.99 1.13
